judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whereas clauses enumerate a long list of purposes (flood reduction, water supply, fisheries, hydroelectric power, pollution abatement) and then trail off into 'and for other purposes', leaving the reach of the recited purposes uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recitals of this kind were used in the fracking litigation to argue that the operative definition of 'project' in Section 1.2(g) and the review power in Section 3.8 reach only water-resource works; that is a classic recital-versus-operative-text tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure naming provision; the stray double period after 'Short title..' is a typographical slip that changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2(c) defining 'Compact' as Part I of the act; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The escape clause 'except as may be otherwise required by the context' makes every defined term contextually variable, which is itself an open-ended and contestable qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on whether 'project' in Section 3.8 must carry the Article 1.2(g) definition, which is exactly the fight the definitions section invites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Area of drainage into the Delaware River and its tributaries, including Delaware Bay' is a definite geographic test with only marginal edge cases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.7's basin-limited jurisdiction and Section 1.2(e)'s 'within or without the basin' language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple naming definition with no evaluative or open-ended term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 2.1 creating the Commission; no inconsistency anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Compact' as Part I of the act, a mechanical cross-reference with no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument repeatedly slips between 'this act' and 'this compact' (e.g., Sections 1.1, 12.13, 14.21), a mild but real drafting inconsistency this definition must absorb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net induced adverse effects, whether or not compensated for' is an economically loaded and boundary-less phrase within a cost definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 11.4 and 12.2 on cost allocation, but nothing there contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facility' piles a sweeping catch-all ('any and all things and appurtenances necessary, useful or convenient', 'or to facilitate any other uses of any of them') onto a list of specifics, squarely raising ejusdem generis/list-scope problems.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is incorporated into the 'project' definition in Section 1.2(g) and into Sections 3.6 and 3.8, so its breadth directly affects the reach of the Commission's review power that was actually litigated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any appropriate branch, department, bureau or division thereof, as the case may be' is loose but is unlikely to be outcome-determinative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with Section 1.2(h) and the federal reservations in Section 15.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'project' is grammatically tangled ('any work, service or activity which is separately planned, financed, or identified by the commission, or any separate facility undertaken ... for the conservation, utilization, control, development or management of water resources'), and whether the qualifying purpose phrase modifies both branches is genuinely contestable; this is the ambiguity litigated over natural gas well pads.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning must be squared with Section 3.8's 'no project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin', with the preamble's water-focused purposes, and with Sections 3.6(b) and 13.1, which pull in different directions on breadth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite membership definition with no evaluative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble's list of parties and Section 14.22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Water and related natural resources in, on, under, or above the ground, including related uses of land, which are subject to beneficial use' is extremely broad and its outer boundary (does it capture subsurface gas, land use generally?) is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the operative limit in Sections 3.8, 3.6(b) and 13.1, so how far it reaches determines the Commission's jurisdiction over activities the preamble never mentions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase carrying no substantive term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It frames findings that are echoed in the preamble; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A declaratory finding of public purpose with no operative test to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.3(b) and 14.3; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statement of sovereign right and joint exercise; declaratory rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside Sections 5.5 and 11.3 reserving state authority, which it broadly matches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A single administrative agency is therefore essential' is a finding, not a rule, and offers little to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably cuts against Section 1.5's directive to preserve existing agencies and Sections 11.1(c)/11.2(c) preserving other agencies' authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A forecast-style finding ('ample to meet all presently projected demands') that states no obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its optimism about supply sits oddly with Article 10's protected-area and emergency shortage machinery, though as a finding it does not truly conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To make secure and protect present developments within the states' and 'equal and uniform treatment to all water users who are similarly situated' are open-textured purpose language used to argue about the Commission's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A purposes clause of this kind pulls against the broad regulatory grants in Sections 3.8 and 10.1, and courts routinely invoke it against expansive readings of those sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard non-derogation clause preserving congressional powers, definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(t) makes the whole federal participation contingent on this section's constitutionality and 15.1(b) is expressly subordinated to it, so its scope has cross-instrument bite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent not inconsistent with the compact' and 'to the fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous' are elastic standards resting on the Commission's own judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) expressly invoke this section as a constraint on Commission operation, while Section 1.3(c) declares a single agency essential — a real pull in two directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal notice window — 'not later than 20 years nor sooner than 25 years prior to the termination' — is awkwardly inverted phrasing that a reader can easily take as an impossible window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the compact sets a termination mechanic, though Section 1.6(b) assumes termination 'by operation of paragraph (a)' which speaks only of notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminated by operation of paragraph (a)' is a compressed cross-reference, since (a) speaks of notice rather than operation, but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves wind-up 'in such manner as may be provided by act of the Congress' even though the states are equal signatories, a mild asymmetry against Sections 1.3(b) and 14.20.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A creation clause with settled corporate-law terms and no evaluative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.1's corporate powers and Section 15.1(m) providing the Commission is not a federal agency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To serve during the term of office of the President' is a definite tenure formula; no ambiguity on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument's own endnote records that this section and Section 15.1(d) ('shall serve at the pleasure of the President') were inconsistent as to the federal member's term until 1997 — an acknowledged internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite appointment and removal mechanics, with the only softness being 'unless otherwise provided by law of the signatory party'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(d) overrides the tenure rule for the federal alternate, and the endnote/WRDA material adds a further designation regime, so the section does not stand alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for necessary expenses' is clear, with 'necessary' the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) expressly permits the federal member and advisor to be paid 'the provisions of Sections 2.4 and 2.6 notwithstanding', a direct carve-out from this rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the membership' can be read as a majority of all seats or of those present, a small but real lexical ambiguity in a voting rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Other provisions require unanimity (Sections 3.3(a), 13.3(b)(2)) or 'a majority of the full membership' (Section 14.5(a)), and the differing formulations invite argument about what this baseline means.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Organizational housekeeping with definite duties; nothing vague enough to litigate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) carves the advisor out of the no-compensation regime and New York's Section 632 elaborates the advisor role, but neither contradicts this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to effectuate its powers or duties within the basin' is an elastic extraterritorial trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the 'within or without the basin' language in Section 1.2(e) and the sale powers in Article 9; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad statement of mission using 'shall develop and effectuate plans, policies and projects', mandatory in form but with no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'projects' in an apparently looser sense than the Section 1.2(g) definition, a small strain against the definitions article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory cross-reference to Article 13.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 13 (Sections 13.1–13.3) tracks the same three instruments, so the cross-reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, definite duty to adopt a comprehensive plan after consultation; 'interested public bodies' is only mildly soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 states the same duty in fuller terms, and the two are consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All public and private projects affecting the basin' and 'such reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' are broad and self-defined boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.2 restates the program requirement with a six-year default period, so the two overlap without squarely conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite budgeting duty with no evaluative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.3 elaborates the same budgets consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Invokes 'the doctrine of equitable apportionment', an external legal standard whose content is contested but which is at least a recognised term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(b) then says no allocation 'shall be deemed to constitute an apportionment of the waters of the basin among the parties', which sits uneasily with an allocation power exercised under the apportionment doctrine.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A state of emergency resulting from a drought or catastrophe' is somewhat open, but the unanimous-consent mechanics are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 3.4, 3.5 and 10.4, and the interlocking decree carve-outs are drafted to be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso preserving covenants 'with a duration not exceeding the life of this compact' is clear, but the disclaimer that no allocation constitutes an apportionment is conceptually strained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably contradicts the opening of Section 3.3, which grants allocation power 'in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any proper party deeming itself aggrieved' leaves 'proper party' undefined anywhere in the compact, and 'out-of-basin diversion' is not defined either.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Proper party' recurs in Section 3.4 without definition and the review route here (Supreme Court original jurisdiction) sits beside the general 'court of competent jurisdiction' route used in Sections 3.8, 10.6 and 15.1(p).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense waiver with nested exceptions and an undefined 'proper party'; the double exception clause is hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with Sections 3.3(a), 3.3(c) and 3.5, and New York's Section 633 adds a further state consent condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To this end, and without limitation thereto' introduces a non-exhaustive list of prohibitions, leaving the reach of the general prohibition uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly subordinates itself to Sections 3.3 and 3.4, and Section 3.8 is in turn made subject to it, so the pieces are designed to interlock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impede or interfere with' rights under the decree is a broad but familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the introductory sentence of Section 3.5 and with Section 3.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on fees for decree-permitted diversions; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 grants a general rate power and Section 15.1(b) adds a further federal restriction, but both are drafted as compatible carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but definite jurisdictional carve-out tied to the decree; 'used in connection with' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 3.8's approval power expressly, so the relationship is stated rather than left implicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence with an explicit consent exception; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the river master consultation contemplated by Section 3.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare permissive introduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere contradicts the framing of Section 3.6 as an enabling list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary, convenient or useful for the purposes of this compact' is an open-ended self-judged standard attached to a long verb string.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth must be reconciled with the limits in Sections 4.5, 9.3 and 3.5 that forbid particular activities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects and facilities in the basin which affect its water resources, including without limitation thereto' followed by enumerated examples is a textbook general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'affect its water resources' trigger is broader than Section 3.8's 'substantial effect' test, and the two standards do not sit easily together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another 'including without limitation thereto' list, but the power is only to research and report, so the catch-all carries little consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(e), 6.4 and 14.12 on data and reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other purposes' is an untethered catch-all at the end of an enumerated list of uses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Section 6.4's warning and posting power; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow investigative power tied to administering the comprehensive plan; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 3.6(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An information and reporting power with no operative test to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps harmlessly with Section 14.12's reporting duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As the commission may deem necessary or desirable' is discretionary but the power to negotiate for aid is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2) on receiving grants and loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other and different powers' plus 'all powers necessary or convenient ... or which may be reasonably implied' is a sweeping catch-all sitting at the end of enumerated specifics, inviting ejusdem generis and expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it could swallow the express limits in Sections 4.5, 9.3 and 3.5, which is precisely the whole-instrument tension a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party' is emphatic and clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) expressly cuts down Section 3.7 for pre-existing free withdrawals and navigation charges, and Section 11.3 reserves state taxing powers, so the section cannot be read alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' turns on two undefined evaluative terms — the scope of 'project' and what counts as a 'substantial effect' — and this is the sentence litigated over natural gas development.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on the Section 1.2(g) definition of 'project' and Section 1.2(i) 'water resources', and it must be squared with the preamble's water-focused purposes and with Sections 3.6(b), 11.1 and 11.2, which use different effect thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'To this end, but with limitation thereto, the commission may' — an evident dropped 'out' that reverses the meaning of the limiting phrase, a mechanical error changing what the provision says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel provisions (Sections 3.5, 4.1, 3.6(b)) all use 'without limitation thereto', confirming the error and creating an inconsistency across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list of cooperative verbs with no evaluative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.5 and 14.1(a)(1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or for any other purpose' is an unbounded catch-all following an enumerated list of engineering functions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.5's direction to employ existing agencies; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So far as consistent with the comprehensive plan' is a soft qualifier but the power itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Sections 13.1 and 3.8, both of which use the comprehensive plan as the touchstone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow enabling power to qualify as a sponsoring agency; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6(g) and Section 15.1(o) limiting other federal agencies' participation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive power to create advisory committees with an illustrative membership list; nothing turns on the list's boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6's advisor mechanism and Section 3.9's coordination duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To this end, without limitation thereto' and 'at such off-river sites as it may find appropriate' leave the scope of the water-supply power open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants power to 'regulate and control the use thereof' while Section 4.5 forbids the Commission from distributing water, a boundary that must be drawn from elsewhere in the article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The purposes list ends with 'and other purposes', an untethered catch-all after enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1 and 3.6(a); no conflicting provision identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No signatory party shall permit any augmentation of flow to be diminished by the diversion of any water' is convoluted double-negative drafting whose operative bite is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exceptions must be read against Section 3.5(b) (decree-permitted diversions), Section 10.3's grandfathered state permits and Section 11.3's reserved state powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specially benefited thereby to a measurable extent' and 'shall not exceed the actual benefit to any water user' are valuation standards with no method supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) restricts charges for withdrawals lawfully free at the effective date and Section 3.5(b) bars charges on decree diversions, both of which cut into this assessment power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short procedural duty to review existing rights and hold a hearing; 'pertinent' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.4(b) enumerates the hearings required and adds a catch-all for 'all other cases wherein this compact requires a public hearing', which absorbs this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Engage in the business of distributing water' is an undefined boundary between permitted transmission facilities and forbidden distribution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 lets the Commission 'regulate and control the use' of its water facilities and Section 2.7 lets it 'sell or dispose of water', so where the prohibition begins is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general enabling power over pollution projects with no evaluative test to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2 and 5.4 and with the federal savings clause in Section 15.1(k).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not injuriously affect waters of the basin as contemplated by the comprehensive plan' is a vague standard that depends entirely on a document outside the section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section 5.5's preservation of state authority and Section 15.1(k)'s preservation of federal water-pollution functions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory condition', 'after reasonable treatment' and 'free from unsightly or malodorous nuisances' are aesthetic and open-textured criteria imposed as a covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges signatories to enact legislation while Section 5.5 preserves their freedom to legislate as they wish; the two pull mildly against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed enforcement mechanics with a 'reasonable time for construction' qualifier; largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Court of competent jurisdiction' is defined differently by New York's Section 634 and by Section 15.1(p), which channels cases to federal district courts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard savings clause; its terms are broad but their direction is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves state authority to impose additional restrictions, while Section 10.8 provides state permits are superseded to the extent of conflict — a genuine tension across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it may deem necessary or desirable' and 'as the commission may deem appropriate' are self-judging but conventional in an enabling grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.2(a) and 3.6(a) on storage and release powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Recommended standards' adopted under a 'power to adopt, amend and repeal' is internally equivocal — are the standards advisory or binding?
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 requires flood-land acquisitions to be 'in accord with the standards adopted and promulgated pursuant to Section 6.2', which presupposes binding force that this subsection disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but procedurally specific; 'encroachment lines' and 'relative risk of flood' are technical rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Article 14 hearings, and Section 14.4(b) supplies compatible notice requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unwarranted constrictions' is a soft term, but the acquisition power itself is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires conformity with Section 6.2 standards that Section 6.2(a) calls merely 'recommended', which leaves the constraint's force uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Lands particularly subject to flood' and 'as conditions may warrant' are loose, but the power is only to post warnings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(d) and 6.2(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sound practices of watershed management' is aspirational language with no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.2 and 7.4 in the same article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short permissive grant using conventional conservation terminology.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Constrained by Section 7.4(b)'s bar on Commission operation, which is expressly cross-referenced within the article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Related to the water resources of the basin' is the only qualifier and it tracks the defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Constrained by Section 7.4(b) in the same article; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general cooperation duty with nothing to apply against a party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated verbatim at Section 8.2(a), which is consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No other suitable unit or agency of government is available to operate the same upon reasonable conditions' is a vague and self-assessed precondition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the operating powers granted in Sections 7.2 and 7.3 and invokes Section 1.5, so the article's grants and this bar must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision moves from a mandatory 'shall provide for the development' to a permissive 'may provide for the construction', an equivocation about what is actually required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made 'subject to the provisions of Section 8.2', which bars the Commission from operating facilities unless no other agency is available — a real constraint on the mandate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general cooperation duty in identical terms to Section 7.4(a); nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.1's cooperative development language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Suitable', 'available' and 'upon reasonable conditions' are all undefined thresholds for a mandatory bar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against Section 8.3(c), which requires the Commission to provide for the operation and maintenance of recreational facilities it owns or controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase; 'within limits prescribed by this article' is a cross-reference, not a standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'limits' are principally Section 8.2(b), which is in some tension with subsection (c) below.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An encouragement and coordination duty with no operative bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9 and 8.2(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Recommend standards' is unmistakably advisory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 6.2(a)'s recommended standards; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite duty to provide for administration and for letting concessions; the terms are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Commission to provide for operating its recreational facilities even though Section 8.2(b) forbids operation where another agency is available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory sealed-bid regime for concessions, definite in its terms apart from the misspelled 'therefore' for 'therefor'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(l) disapplies this section to facilities operated under other federal law, and Section 14.9 allows competitive bidding to be waived in listed cases — differing regimes for Commission contracting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive impoundment authorisation tied to the comprehensive plan; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.2 and 13.1; Section 1.4 preserves congressional navigable-waters powers over the same waters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enabling power with no evaluative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 9.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Where such facilities are not otherwise available upon reasonable terms' and the bar on 'the business of direct sale to consumers' both draw lines whose location is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.7 authorises the Commission to 'sell or dispose of ... hydroelectric power' within or without the basin, which sits awkwardly with the direct-sale prohibition here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable terms, consideration and duration' is an open-ended standard governing contracts of potentially long life.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.2's authorisation power and Section 14.4(b)'s hearing requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and just' is the classic vague rate standard with no benchmark supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 lets the Commission fix rates 'without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party', which leaves unclear who enforces this constraint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad delegation power exercised as the Commission 'may deem necessary or desirable'; the discretion is wide but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York's Section 637 restricts acceptance of delegations under this section, and Section 10.8 sets out how state systems yield, so this power is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Have developed or threaten to develop to such a degree as to create a water shortage' is a predictive and boundary-less trigger for protected-area status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 and 10.6, which build on the same designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grandfather clause for permits 'heretofore granted under the laws of any of the signatory states' is an exception whose temporal reach and durability are unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.8 provides that state-issued diversion and withdrawal permits are superseded to the extent of conflict, which is difficult to square with the exception preserved here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad emergency prohibition on withdrawal 'for any purpose', definite in form though drastic in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Section 10.3 it contains no grandfather for existing state permits, and Section 3.5(b)/3.3(a) protect decree diversions, so its interaction with those provisions is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Just and equitable interests and rights of other lawful users' and 'due regard to the need to balance and reconcile alternative and conflicting uses' supply no administrable rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties permitting to the comprehensive plan, consistently with Sections 3.8 and 13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short judicial-review clause; 'Section 10.3 through 10.5' is a slightly loose citation but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York's Section 634 gives 'court of competent jurisdiction' a special meaning for this subsection, and Section 15.1(p) channels compact cases to federal district courts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A record-keeping duty defined entirely by what the Commission prescribes; definite in mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 and 11.5 on state cooperation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whenever the commission finds it necessary or desirable' makes supersession turn on the Commission's own unreviewed view, and 'to the extent of any conflict' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely cuts against Section 10.3(ii)'s preservation of previously granted state permits and against Section 5.5's savings clause for state authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory purpose statement subject to Section 1.4; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its subordination to Section 1.4 and Section 15.1(s) shapes how the following rules bind federal agencies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects related to powers delegated to the commission' is a broad and undefined class of federal projects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on the contested Section 1.2(g) 'project' definition and is subordinated to Section 1.4 and Section 15.1(s).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nor shall it be deemed authorized' is a strong and unusual formulation whose effect on separately authorised federal projects is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is difficult to reconcile with Section 11.1(c), which preserves each federal agency's existing authority, and with Sections 1.4 and 15.1(s)'s presidential override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' is a definite carve-back, though its interaction with the preceding paragraphs is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves federal agency authority that Section 11.1(b) appears to negate, a tension the section does not itself resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory purpose statement with no operative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 11.1's introduction; the substance lies in the following paragraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects related to powers delegated to the commission' repeats the same broad, undefined class for state projects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope again turns on the litigated Section 1.2(g) definition of 'project'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on state and local expenditure absent inclusion in the comprehensive plan; definite but extremely broad in reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with Section 11.2(c) preserving state and local agency authority and with Section 5.5's savings clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the very authority that Section 11.2(b) purports to condition on inclusion in the comprehensive plan.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short reservation of taxing power in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 allows the Commission to set charges 'without regulation or control by any ... agency of any signatory party' and Section 14.3 exempts the Commission from state taxation, so the boundary of this reservation is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Equitable cost sharing and reimbursement formulas' states an aim without a method, but the list that follows gives it content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(a) and 13.3, which assume cost sharing plans prepared under this article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A procedural item in a list; 'uniform and consistent' is aspirational but unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2(d)'s cost definition and Section 13.3's budgeting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list item authorising contracts for shared financial responsibility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20 and 14.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An accounting-mechanics item with no evaluative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.3 and 14.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payments in lieu of taxes' is a defined concept elsewhere in the instrument and the item is procedural.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.3 prescribes a specific in-lieu payment regime for ten years, which this open-ended apportionment power overlaps.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within the limits of available appropriations' and 'whenever the parties deem appropriate' make the pledge largely self-cancelling, which is a genuine drafting softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(h) expressly overrides this section for federal agencies, limiting their pledge to what they agree to or the President directs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section says bonds are 'payable solely out of the properties and revenues of the commission without recourse to taxation' and in the next breath calls them 'direct and general obligations' backed by the Commission's 'full faith and credit', two characterisations that sit awkwardly together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.3 bars pledging any signatory's credit and Section 15.1(g) disclaims any US obligation, which are consistent, but the internal 'solely'/'general obligation' pairing still needs harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The purpose of this compact shall include without limitation thereto all costs of any project' is grammatically garbled — purposes do not 'include costs' — and the sentence evidently means the purposes for which bonds may be issued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is meant to expand 'any of the purposes of this compact' in Section 12.1, but read literally it enlarges the compact's purposes generally, which would spill into Sections 3.6(a) and 14.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat exclusion of credit and personal liability, stated in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1, 12.20 and 15.1(g).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed refunding mechanics with no evaluative standard beyond 'deems it expedient'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence expressly incorporates all bond provisions of the compact, so it fits Sections 12.5 and 12.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but mechanical authorisation language; nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6, 12.7 and 12.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long enumeration of permissible indenture covenants, but each item is concrete and the list is expressly non-exhaustive by design.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for 'any restriction on the regulatory powers vested in the commission' preserves Sections 3.7 and 14.2, so it is drafted to fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No bond or its terms shall mature in more than fifty years from its own date' is clumsy — terms do not mature — and 'its own date' is defined only by the face of the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6 on maturities; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Free and exempt from all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties, except for transfer, inheritance and estate taxes' is definite in form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 1.2(h) makes the federal government a 'signatory party', this exemption on its face covers federal taxation, which Section 15.1(f) expressly denies — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence leaving the rate wholly to the Commission; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As amended in 1984 it removed a rate ceiling, yet Section 12.13 still caps net interest cost at six percent for below-par sales, leaving a residual mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple permissive provision on place and currency of payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard facsimile-signature and continuity-of-signature language, well settled in bond practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.5 on officers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence power to repurchase and resell its own bonds; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4 and 12.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section commands that all cash bonds 'shall be sold on sealed proposals to the highest bidder' and then permits private sale after rejection, an internal tension compounded by the fixed six-percent formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.20(b) allows bonds to be delivered to signatory agencies 'notwithstanding any other provision of this compact' without public offering, and Section 12.9 as amended leaves the rate to the Commission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short negotiability rule with a clear registration exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6 on registered and coupon forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short declaration of legal-investment status; its terms are standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to bind state investment law directly, which fits the states' concurring legislation but not the federal reservations in Section 15.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conclusive against all persons whomsoever' is sweeping but unmistakable in intent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12.5's validity provisions; the in rem procedure is left to signatory law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording and pledge-effectiveness rules stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.18 on pledged revenues.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence structure is tangled — an exception for 'expenses for other purposes including ... or other purposes' embedded before the operative prohibition — so the scope of the trust fund restriction is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Sections 12.6 and 3.7 on rates and revenues, but no contrary provision was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of bondholder remedies closed by an express non-exclusivity sentence, which defuses the usual expressio unius problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Court of competent jurisdiction of any signatory party' must be read with Section 15.1(p) and New York's Section 634.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The signatory parties will provide such capital funds' followed by 'nothing in this section shall be deemed to impose any mandatory obligation' is a self-cancelling undertaking on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.3(c) has the parties 'covenant and agree' to fund the current expense budget, so the compact treats capital and expense contributions inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any other provision of this compact' is clear in effect though it leaves the reader to work out what it displaces.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It plainly overrides Section 12.13's mandatory sealed-bid public sale requirement, an override the reader must locate for themselves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly permissive funding provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(g), 14.1(a)(2) and 14.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All public and private projects and facilities which are required, in the judgment of the commission, for the optimum planning ... of the water resources of the basin' hangs the plan's contents on the same contested word 'projects' and on the vague 'optimum'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Inclusion in this plan is the trigger for Sections 11.1(b) and 11.2(b) and the touchstone for Section 3.8 approval, so its breadth is bound up with the litigated scope of Commission jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The ensuing six years or such other reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' lets the Commission set its own horizon, a soft but disclosed discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.2(b) states the same duty without the six-year default, a small mismatch between the two statements of the program requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single list item with no operative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tracks Section 3.2(b) exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All public and private projects to be anticipated' is a broad but purely descriptive planning requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.2(b)'s 'all public and private projects affecting the basin'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list item requiring a separate statement; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tracks Section 3.2(b) and Section 13.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite annual budgeting duty with specified contents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.2(c) and 13.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Apportioned equitably among the signatory parties' supplies no formula, and the unanimity requirement gives every party a veto over an obligation the section treats as mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unanimous-vote rule departs from the majority rule in Section 2.5, and the resulting apportionment sits against Section 12.20(a)'s disclaimer of mandatory obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Covenant and agree to include ... subject to such review and approval as may be required by their respective budgetary processes' makes the covenant conditional on the promisor's own later decision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its enforceability question is compounded by Section 12.20(a)'s express denial of mandatory obligations and by the endnote's WRDA funding directives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare permissive introduction to a list of corporate powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1 and 3.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Enter intro contracts' contains an obvious typographical error, though the intended meaning is recoverable; 'sue and be sued in all courts of competent jurisdiction' is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York's Section 634 gives 'court of competent jurisdiction' in this very item a special state-law meaning, and Section 15.1(p) channels compact cases federally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly worded receiving power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(g), 12.20(c) and 14.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short planning and specification power with no evaluative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9(c) and 3.6(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line control power over the Commission's own facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.7 and 4.1, though Section 4.5 forbids water distribution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it may deem necessary' and 'necessary, useful or convenient' are self-judged standards, but the property powers themselves are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.14 and 14.15 on acquisition and conveyance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All corporate powers essential to the declared objects and purposes' is a residual catch-all at the end of an enumerated list, inviting ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the implied-powers catch-all in Section 3.6(h), and both must be read against the express prohibitions in Sections 4.5, 9.3 and 3.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introduction, qualified only by 'subject to the provisions of this compact'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5 and 14.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as otherwise provided by or pursuant to this compact' is a standard saving formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5, 14.5(a) and 10.1's delegation power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to any provisions of law specifically applicable to agencies or instrumentalities created by compact' is vague as to which laws are meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) provides the Commission is not a federal agency for various statutes, which bears on which laws apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short internal-administration power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.6 and 14.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Principal officers' is left undefined but the appointment power is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.5(a) gives the executive director power to appoint all other officers and employees, so the boundary of 'principal officers' matters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it deems necessary' and 'subject to the provisions of this article' are soft but ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 14.5(b) and 14.8, which constrain appointment and removal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line contracting power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Constrained by Sections 14.9 and 8.4 on competitive bidding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare permissive introduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere conflicts with the framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable rules and regulations' and the exception for rules 'which deal solely with the internal management of the commission' are both open-textured qualifiers on a rulemaking power backed by penalties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The filing requirement depends on each signatory's administrative law, and Section 14.17 attaches penalties to rules whose validity turns on that filing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Investigator or watchman' vested with 'the powers of a peace officer of the state' is a terse conferral of coercive authority whose scope is left to state law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Sections 5.4 and 14.17 on enforcement, but no state-law-facing provision defines the resulting powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The in-lieu payment formula is hard to parse — payments equal to the taxes for 'the tax year next prior to its acquisition ... for a period of ten years' — and the review standard ('hardships incurred and benefits received') is wholly evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.3 reserves state taxing powers and Section 11.4(d) contemplates apportioned payments in lieu of taxes, so three provisions address the same subject on different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All meetings of the commission shall be open to the public' is absolute and unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves no room for the executive sessions that Section 2.6's self-organisation power and Section 14.1(b) deliberations might otherwise assume.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In all other cases wherein this compact requires a public hearing' is a catch-all after an enumerated list, though it works in the inclusive direction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must gather the hearing requirements scattered across Sections 3.7, 4.4, 5.2, 6.2(b), 8.4, 9.4, 10.2, 10.4, 13.1 and 14.2, which use varying formulations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line public-records rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.4(a) and 14.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the full membership' is precise, and the appointment structure is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.5 requires only 'a majority of the membership' for Commission action, and the differing formulations invite argument about which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No political, racial, religious or residence test' is an enumerated list that may exclude other prohibited criteria by implication, and 'merit and fitness' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.8(b) prescribes forfeiture for wilful violations while this section requires removal for any violation found by the Commission, a difference in trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite oath requirement with a fixed fifteen-day deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.5(a) on appointments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such bond and in such form and amount as the commission may require' is wholly discretionary but unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.5 and 14.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare prohibitory introduction naming the covered persons.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It covers commissioners, whereas the sanction in Section 14.8(b) reaches only officers and employees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Financially interested, either directly or indirectly' is a boundary-less conflict standard with no de minimis or disclosure exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.8(c) voids contracts made in contravention, which magnifies the indeterminacy of 'indirectly'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Money or any other thing of value' is broad but the prohibition is intelligible; 'within the scope of his official duties' is a familiar line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) permits federal compensation to the US member notwithstanding Section 2.4, which brushes against this prohibition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow and plainly worded anti-bribery rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.8(b) and (d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sanction reaches 'any officer or employee' and adds a wilfulness element, both of which narrow the class and conduct covered by subsection (a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (a) prohibits conduct by 'commissioner, officer or employee', so commissioners are subject to the prohibition but not to this forfeiture — an unexplained gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowingly made in contravention of this section is void' leaves unclear whose knowledge counts and whether innocent counterparties lose their bargain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the bond and contract powers in Sections 14.1(a) and 12.6, where third parties rely on validity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cumulative-sanctions clause referring outward to federal and state law; plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.17 and 15.1(n), which addresses the federal status of Commission personnel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Lowest responsible bidder', 'a manner reasonably likely to attract prospective bidders' and 'financially responsible' are undefined qualitative tests governing a mandatory bidding regime.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 imposes a different sealed-bid regime for concessions and Section 12.13 another for bonds, while Section 12.20(b) overrides bidding for bonds sold to signatory agencies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An objective exemption identified by counterparty; nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.5 and 3.9(b) on employing other governmental agencies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The public exigency requires the immediate delivery' is a wholly evaluative and self-judged trigger for waiving competitive bidding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.4's emergency machinery uses a different and more formal trigger, but the two operate in separate spheres.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only one source of supply is available' is a factual test, though 'available' has some elasticity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Section 14.9's waiver list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Of a technical nature' and 'necessary in order to assure standardization ... in the public interest' pile three open-ended judgments into one waiver ground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other waiver grounds in Section 14.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Services ... of a specialized or professional nature' is the vaguest item in the waiver list and sits at its end, functioning as a catch-all that could swallow the bidding rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It undercuts the mandatory sealed-bid requirement in the same section's opening sentence, a tension internal to Section 14.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pay the premiums therefore' misuses 'therefore' for 'therefor', and 'loss of revenue from any cause whatsoever' is a sweeping but permissive phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its subordination to bond agreements ties it to Section 12.6's insurance covenants, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practical' (for 'practicable') and 'no personal interest direct or indirect' are soft, and the section sets no audit deadline at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 14.11(b), (c) and New York's Section 640 add overlapping audit rights, which coexist rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All other papers, things or property of the commission' is a sweeping catch-all appended to an enumerated list of records.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York's Section 640 channels this right to the state comptroller, and Section 15.1(q) reserves separate congressional disclosure rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short provision subjecting the Commission's transactions to GAO audit under comptroller general rules; definite in terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It treats the Commission like a federal instrumentality even though Section 15.1(m) provides that for stated purposes 'the commission shall not be considered a Federal agency', and Section 14.11(a) already provides for independent audit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Refuse to give all require assistance' is ungrammatical — plainly a dropped 'd' from 'required' — in a clause that imposes automatic forfeiture of office.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the forfeiture sanction in Section 14.8(b) but applies without any wilfulness requirement, an inconsistency in the compact's disciplinary standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain annual-reporting duty plus a discretionary publication power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(f) and 14.4(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare permissive introduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Preliminary expenses such as' introduces an illustrative list whose outer boundary is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.2 and 12.20(c) on funding purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient' is soft but the advancing power itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.13(b) on repayment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For benefits received or to be received' is broad but the payment power is permissive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.3 and 11.4 on benefit-based charges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repayment terms are left entirely to later agreement, which leaves the obligation indefinite but transparently so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.20(a); no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Includes but is not limited to' introduces a catch-all, and the exclusion 'other than property of a signatory party and any property held ... in connection with a diversion authorized by a United States Supreme Court decree' is awkwardly conjoined and hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with Section 3.5(c)'s bar on Commission jurisdiction over decree-related facilities and with Section 14.15's separate conveyance machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear choice-of-procedure rule with an express fallback to state condemnation law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 15.1(m) and 15.1(p) on the Commission's federal/state posture, though those complicate which law is 'applicable'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat allocation of liability for condemnation awards; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.3 and 12.20(a) on the parties' non-liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to the effectuation of the authorized purposes' is soft, but the provision only authorises conveyances.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.1(a)(5) and 14.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Authorized and empowered ... to grant and convey ... upon the commission's request' leaves genuinely unclear whether a political subdivision must convey when asked or merely may.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.14(a) provides a condemnation route for property 'already devoted to a public use', which suggests conveyance here is voluntary — but the 'upon request' phrasing points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not in any event exceed the expenditure required to serve the public convenience and necessity' is an undefined ceiling on relocation costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 14.14(a)'s public-utility carve-out, which turns on whether the facility 'is to be relocated or replaced'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to such reasonable conditions as the highway department ... may require' is a familiar reasonableness qualifier on an otherwise clear grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.14 and 14.15; state highway authority is preserved rather than displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Punishable as may be provided by statute of any of the signatory parties within which the offense is committed' mixes 'any' with a single-jurisdiction test, and the default $50–$1,000 penalty is left to be 'fixed by the court'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It attaches criminal-type consequences to rules whose validity depends on the filing requirement in Section 14.2(a) and to orders reviewable under Section 5.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers, agents and employees of the government of the United States' imports an entire federal liability regime by reference, with no indication which statutes are meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) provides the Commission is not a federal agency for the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes it cites, so the borrowed regime and the disclaimer point in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause; 'affecting or intending to affect or in any way to interfere with' is redundant but directionally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 10's withdrawal permits, Section 4.2(b)'s diversion bar and Section 14.14(a)'s power to condemn 'riparian rights' all plainly affect riparian rights under state law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Amendments and supplements ... to implement the purposes thereof' limits amendment by an undefined purposive test, and unanimity is required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(q) reserves to Congress the unilateral 'right to alter, amend, or repeal this Act', and Section 1.4 recognises unilateral federal modification — hard to square with a unanimity rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'It is the legislative intent that the provisions of such compact be reasonably and liberally construed' is itself a construction directive that parties fight over, and 'reasonably' pulls against 'liberally'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(t) provides that invalidity of Section 1.4 ends US participation altogether, which is the opposite of the general severability declared here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Thirty days after the enactment of concurring legislation' is a definite trigger, and the execution mechanics are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The concurring state acts and Section 15.3 each say 'this act shall take effect immediately', which sits awkwardly with the thirty-day rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory conditions clause tied to Section 1.4; no operative term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It subordinates the whole compact to the reservations that follow, several of which override named compact sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Beyond the planning stage' is an undefined threshold, and the carve-out for 'a project for which State supplied funds only will be used' turns on a funding characterisation that may change over time.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Requiring an Act of Congress for every project cuts deeply into the Commission's operational powers in Articles 3 through 9 and its plan under Section 13.1, a whole-instrument tension the compact never resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'impose any change for water withdrawals or diversions' where 'charge' is plainly meant — a mechanical error in the operative verb of the restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts down Section 3.7's rate power and overlaps Section 3.5(b) and Section 11.3, and its own proviso subordinates it to Section 1.4, leaving a layered set of qualifications.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The executive powers of the President in the event of a national emergency' is an undefined and contested body of authority invoked without limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 10.4's emergency machinery and Section 15.1(s)'s presidential override without saying how they interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve at the pleasure of the President' is unambiguous on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact's own endnote records that this provision and Section 2.2 ('during the term of office of the President') were inconsistent until 1997 — an expressly acknowledged internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impairing or in any manner affecting the applicability to all Federal funds budgeted and appropriated for use by the commission' is missing its object — the applicability of what? — so the sentence does not parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on Sections 12.20 and 13.3(c) concerning federal contributions, and the WRDA endnote adds further funding directives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Are or may continued to be free or exempt' is ungrammatical (a dropped 'continue'), in the operative comparison that defines the exemption's scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8 exempts Commission bonds from 'all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties', and the federal government is a signatory party under Section 1.2(h) — a direct clash this paragraph is trying to fix.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and unmistakable disclaimer of federal obligation, legal or moral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.3, which limit recourse to Commission revenues.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pledged only to the extent that the respective agencies shall from time to time agree' converts a pledge into a discretion, but says so openly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides Section 11.5's pledge of technical and administrative services, and sits against Section 15.2(b)'s directive that agencies 'shall cooperate with and furnish appropriate assistance'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In excess of eight hours in any workday or forty hours in any workweek, as the case may be' leaves the overtime trigger genuinely uncertain, and the string of statutory citations contains an unclosed parenthesis.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It attaches wage conditions to Commission contracting that Section 14.9's bidding regime does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short threshold rule incorporating a named statute; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $10,000 figure matches Section 14.9's construction threshold but not its $2,500 supplies threshold, a minor mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph says federal water-pollution functions are not limited by the compact and then provides that the exercise of those functions 'shall not limit the authority of the commission' — a circular pair in which neither yields.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 5.2, 5.4 and 5.5, which already divide pollution authority between the Commission and the signatories, leaving three overlapping regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence disapplication of a named section; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves federally operated facilities out of Section 8.4's mandatory concession bidding, an exception the reader must find in Part II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense list of statutory citations, but its operative statement — the Commission is not a federal agency for those purposes — is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.18 makes the Commission liable in tort only as federal officers and employees are, which is difficult to operate once the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes are disapplied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical exclusions ('advisors, and personnel employed by the United States member under direct Federal appropriation') are clumsily punctuated but intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 14.5 and 15.1(r), which permit federal compensation of the US member and advisor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-enlargement clause with no evaluative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.1(c) and 15.1(s)1, which preserve rather than enlarge federal agency authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All cases or controversies arising under the Compact' is a broad jurisdictional formula, and the immunity sentence sits oddly beside the grant of jurisdiction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact repeatedly commits review to 'any court of competent jurisdiction' (Sections 3.8, 4.3, 5.4, 10.6) and New York's Section 634 defines that phrase as the state supreme court, which this exclusive federal grant unsettles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As is deemed appropriate by the Congress or any such committee' is entirely self-judged, but the reservation itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unilateral right to alter, amend or repeal is hard to reconcile with Section 14.20's requirement of concurrence by all signatories and with Section 1.6's fixed duration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the rates which he shall deem to prevail in respect to comparable officers' is discretionary but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly displaces Sections 2.4 and 2.6's no-compensation rule for the federal member and advisor, and the WRDA endnote adds that the ex-officio member serves 'without additional compensation'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not substantially conflict' is an undefined threshold, 'United Sates' is a misspelling, and the two nested provisos partly undo the opening declaration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions the operation of Section 3.8 and Article 11 on presidential concurrence and lets the President delete parts of the Section 13.1 comprehensive plan, which cuts across the Commission's core powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At any time between the first and sixtieth day of the sixth year after the initial adoption ... and of every sixth year thereafter' is a convoluted window that is easy to compute two ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the concurrence mechanism presupposed by paragraph 1 and interacts with the annual revision powers in Section 13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except to the extent that the President deems remaining a party necessary and proper to protect the national interest' creates a partial-withdrawal state whose content is entirely undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.21 declares the compact's provisions severable, while this paragraph makes the invalidity of Section 1.4 fatal to US participation — the two severability regimes conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent ... are hereby amended ... to the extent necessary' is an implied-amendment formula of undefined reach, followed by a proviso pulling the other way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 15.1(k)'s preservation of other federal water-pollution functions and Section 15.1(o)'s non-enlargement rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such action as may be necessary and proper, in his discretion' is broad but is a standard effectuation formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored in the Delaware, New Jersey and Pennsylvania effectuation sections; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall cooperate with and furnish appropriate assistance' is mandatory in form but 'appropriate' leaves the content open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(h) states that federal technical services are pledged only so far as agencies agree or the President directs, which contradicts the mandatory 'shall cooperate' here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading reads 'Effect Date' rather than 'Effective Date', a mechanical slip in an otherwise one-line provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'This Act shall take effect immediately' sits against Section 14.22, under which the compact becomes binding thirty days after all concurring legislation is enacted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All acts and parts of acts inconsistent with any provision of this act' repeals an unidentified body of law by reference, leaving its reach to be worked out case by case.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels New York's Section 641 and Section 15.1(u), which use different formulations for the same effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such action as may be necessary and proper, in his discretion' is a standard and openly discretionary effectuation formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical in substance to Section 15.2(a) and the New Jersey and Pennsylvania counterparts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line effective-date provision with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Take effect immediately' sits against Section 14.22's rule that the compact becomes binding thirty days after all concurring legislation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same open-ended repealer language, with the repealed body of law unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Delaware and Pennsylvania repealers and New York's Section 641; consistent among themselves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard discretionary effectuation authorisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 15.2(a) and the other states' effectuation sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line effective-date provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'immediately' does not sit easily with Section 14.22's thirty-day trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence refers to 'the alternate of said department head on the water resources commission' although no department head has been mentioned — a broken antecedent in a succession rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.3 of the compact contemplates a single alternate appointed by the member, so this second-level substitute has no obvious compact basis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in its designation of the mayor and in the notice condition for designees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6 leaves the advisor's appointment to 'each member in his discretion', which this section removes for New York — a state-law override of a compact discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference to 'subdivision three of section three of article three of the compact' does not map cleanly onto Section 3.3's lettered paragraphs, and the consent described is that in Section 3.3(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions New York's compact consent on prior approval of a state body, a layer the compact's Section 3.3(a) unanimity rule does not contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives one phrase three different meanings for different compact sections, and the descriptive cross-references ('item one of paragraph (a) of subdivision one of section fourteen of article fourteen') are hard to verify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(p) gives United States district courts original jurisdiction over all cases arising under the compact, which cuts against this state-court definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Whether a 'project requires approval of the Delaware River Basin Commission' turns entirely on the contested compact definition, so the trigger is only as definite as that term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends on Sections 1.2(g) and 3.8 — the very provisions whose scope was litigated — and it makes state permits hostage to that scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grant of municipal power with a savings clause; both parts are plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 6.2(b)'s technical and financial aid agreements accurately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional bar on accepting delegations, tied to whether the body would otherwise have the power; definite though counterfactual in form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 10.1's delegation power for New York agencies, a limit the compact itself does not state.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within the limits of available appropriations' makes the duty conditional but says so plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 11.5's pledge, and Section 15.1(h) qualifies only the federal side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'During the ensuring fiscal year' is a plain misspelling of 'ensuing' in the operative budget period, and 'estimate of moneys required' is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes budgeting through the state director of the budget while Section 13.3(b) has the executive director transmit certified budgets and apportionments directly, two overlapping procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short audit authorisation with a discretionary scope ('as such comptroller may deem proper').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It implements Section 14.11(b)'s examination right accurately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No provision of the conservation law or of any other law, which is inconsistent with the provisions of the compact' is an open-ended disapplication with a stray comma that obscures the restrictive clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Delaware, New Jersey and Pennsylvania repealers and Section 15.1(u), each using different language for the same displacement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section twice directs the governor to act 'as provided in said subdivision twenty-one of section fourteen of article fourteen', but the compact's signing, sealing and filing rules are in Section 14.22, not Section 14.21 (Construction and Severability) — a cross-reference error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it points New York's effectuation at the severability clause, which cannot be reconciled with Section 14.22's execution and filing requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line effective-date provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Immediately' sits against Section 14.22's thirty-day binding rule and against Section 2 of the same New York act, which defers effectiveness to Section 14.22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same open-ended repealer formula with the repealed law unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Delaware and New Jersey repealers; consistent among themselves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard discretionary effectuation authorisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 15.2(a) and the other states' equivalents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line effective-date provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Immediately' again sits against Section 14.22's thirty-day rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An explanatory endnote rather than an operative term; it quotes and paraphrases amending statutes without imposing obligations of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly states that Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d) 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment', and the quoted WRDA operates 'notwithstanding ... Section 2.2', so the instrument as printed still contains superseded text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quoted federal directive with detailed notification mechanics; the only softness is 'to fulfill the equitable funding requirements'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges the Secretary to allocate 'an amount equal to the amount determined by the Commission' under Section 13.3(b), while Section 12.20(a) denies any mandatory obligation and paragraph (3) contemplates non-allocation — an unresolved funding tension.
